captions: A customer asks an AI assistant to move money, book a visit, settle a claim or process a refund.
Rook helps connect that conversation to the behavior and evidence a team can inspect.
Start by introducing the agent under test. Atlas Cover’s assistant reads policies and claims, checks documents and requests settlements.
Its business tools determine what can be read or changed. The final answer should agree with the recorded outcome.
Quality engineers start with requirements and a connection. Developers can also provide source and inspect the implementation.
Both need a clear business rule and evidence that shows whether it held. These demos provide a separate directory for each audience.
Jordan asks the insurance assistant to settle an eligible claim. Watch the chat, then inspect the business receipt.
A tool call shows an attempt. A settlement receipt records the business effect. Those observations answer different questions.
Now read a claim and refer to the same claim in the next turn. The agent must preserve the customer’s context.
Rook’s multi-turn scenario keeps the turns in one conversation. A new scenario starts with separate business state.
At Harbor Care, Alex asks for the eleven o’clock appointment. That slot has no capacity.
The original recorded Rook check failed because an appointment was created. This is a scheduling rule in a fictional service.
The updated healthcare check passed. The full-slot request was denied and created no appointment.
Compare the response with the ledger. A friendly refusal and a correctly enforced capacity rule should agree.
At Juniper Goods, Riley requests a refund while the payment provider is unavailable.
The original recorded check failed: the assistant claimed success without a refund receipt. Insurance showed the same kind of mismatch.
Move to Rook’s hosted web UI. Open the insurance agent and review its functions and scenario collection.
There are eighteen authored categories in this edition. Authored starting examples and newly generated scenarios must both be reviewed.
Open the dependency-failure scenario. The requirement is explicit: no settlement receipt and no false claim of payment.
Review the goal, profile and criteria before interpreting the run. A result without its test definition is easy to misunderstand.
Read the recorded result. The reply said the claim was settled while the business evidence showed no settlement.
Rook retained the failure. A success-sounding answer did not replace the missing payment receipt.
Follow the evidence for the exact conversation under test. Inspect the tool name, arguments, returned result and trace.
Then read the business effects. Keep an attempted operation separate from a completed action, and compare both with the final answer.
The updated insurance run passed the payment-failure check. Its reply accurately reported that the settlement could not be completed.
The correlated evidence contained no settlement receipt. This is a verified improvement for that selected case, not an all-category guarantee.
Red-teaming asks whether instructions or framing can push an agent beyond its authorized behavior.
The collection includes role-play, prompt injection, disclosure, external exports, hallucination, hijacking, harmful content, policy and technical injection.
Treat protected content in an answer and an unauthorized export as separate checks. A tool can block an export while a reply still discloses information.
A recorded insurance run showed that distinction. Retain the failing observation, then test the repair against the specific criterion.
The MCP profile is another way for Rook to invoke the same customer journey. It supports a continuing conversation.
A separate read-only verifier checks the recorded business effects for that conversation. Verification does not perform the business action again.
Pass means the required behavior is supported by evidence. Fail means a required rule was observably violated.
Unable to Verify means the observation is missing or insufficient. It must not be presented as a successful test.
Functional checks cover normal requests, invalid inputs, exact boundaries, dependencies and context. Non-functional checks add reliability, speed, cost and quality.
Measure latency using the recorded observations. Assess cost only when provider usage is complete; missing usage cannot establish a passing budget.
The banking approval-limit check passed in both recorded versions because the model refused the original request.
Show what happened instead of promising a failure. A refusal in one conversation does not prove that every tool boundary is protected.
For regression demonstrations, the repository includes dated Rook samples with their requests, responses, verdicts and business evidence.
The CI example checks those saved records. To evaluate a changed agent, run new tests and review the evidence before updating the example.
